headline: Council committee reviews emergency agency's fiscal year 27 budget

meeting.body: Maui County Council Budget, Finance, and Economic Development Committee
meeting.summary: A council committee questioned the emergency agency's budget, including $1 million for wildfire fuel removal and a new emergency center expected in June.
meeting.recap: The committee continued its review of the proposed fiscal year 27 budget for the County of Maui.[[0:18:47]] The emergency management agency asked for $1 million to remove hazardous fuels, meaning plants that can feed wildfires.[[0:24:50]] The agency's administrator said clearing 10 parcels, about 1,100 acres of grass, would cost about $3.3 million.[[0:25:18]] The agency plans to use a remaining $150,000 for a strategic plan for community resiliency hubs.[[0:28:52]] Funding for agency office space on Molokaʻi and in East Maui is identified, but no space is agreed on yet.[[0:31:24]] A council member asked about funding to get stores' perishable food to people during outages.[[0:46:04]] The administrator said the budget includes $380,000 to support emergency activations.[[0:46:44]] The chair said a presidential disaster declaration was signed, which members had waited for to get federal funding.[[0:52:20]] The administrator said the County has deconstructed 30,000 pounds of electric vehicle batteries for disposal.[[1:27:46]] Members may send more questions for the department by nine o'clock tomorrow morning.[[1:35:08]] The committee took a recess, with a different department to follow.[[1:35:48]]
meeting.next: The administrator said the agency needs to follow up on the status of an office space in East Maui. A flood coordinator position is part of the fiscal year 27 proposal and will be pursued once approved. The agency is working to set up an end-of-life program for electric vehicle batteries. After the break, the committee planned to come back to talk with another department.

issues.oneLine: A council member asked whether the County could fund getting stores' perishable food to people during outages.
issues.why: The member said East Maui was without electricity for about three days during the first storm.
issues.next: The administrator said they would have to check on that situation.
issues.brief: The member said one store has an agreement to give its perishable food to Red Cross for shelters.[[#1]] The administrator said $380,000 for activations could go to items like refrigeration trailers and generators.[[#2]]

issues.oneLine: A presidential disaster declaration was signed, opening the way for federal funding.
issues.why: The chair said the declaration was what members were waiting for in order to get federal funding.
issues.next: The administrator said the agency and the Office of Recovery will improve how they coordinate moving forward.
issues.brief: The administrator said this is the first time the Office of Recovery has been part of the shift from response to recovery.[[#1]] The administrator said the declaration enables a public assistance program and a hazard mitigation program.[[#2]] County departments apply for projects under these programs.[[#3]]
